thread:
chloe: heads-up  customer Cetus uploaded LoRA v0.2 and i merged into `cust/cetus/lora-staging`. QA flagged a weird token-boundary regression: enumerated lists sometimes drop the leading digit or merge the number with the following token. blocking onboarding sign-off.

rahul: can you paste a minimal repro from the smoke set?

chloe: sure, from evals/cetus_smoke_140.json:
```
Prompt: "List the 3 prerequisites to enroll."
Gold: "1) Valid account
2) Verified email
3) Agreement accepted"
Merged: ") Valid account
1) Verified email
2) Agreement accepted"  <-- leading '1' lost for first item
```

mai: interesting. not the usual sentencepiece mismatch. Cetus used a byte-level BPE tokenizer (noted in their README) and they also applied a numeric-token compaction step during finetune (they compacted multi-digit numerics into a single token id range).

ben: that numeric compaction can collide with our special token indices if the LoRA assumes a different numeric-token offset. Did you inspect lora_meta.json?

chloe: yes: "\"tokenizer\":\"byte_bpe\",\"numeric_compaction\":true, \"special_tokens_order\":[\"PAD\",\"UNK\",\"BOS\",\"EOS\"]". Our serving model `redwood-b3-bpe` has `special_tokens_order` `[BOS,EOS,PAD,UNK]` and no numeric compaction. The merge left merged vocab size unchanged but the numeric-id block was shifted by +2 which explains the lost leading digit (it mapped to PAD id).

rahul: ouch. two separate problems: special-token ordering mismatch and compacted numeric-token id space. We need a deterministic remap that preserves numeric glyph tokens to the correct ids before merging.

mai: suggestion: extend `tools/token_remap.py` with a `--preserve-numeric-range` flag that detects numeric-token ranges in the source LoRA and assigns them to a non-overlapping numeric token range in the target, preserving relative ids. Also explicitly remap specials to the canonical order.

chloe: i prototyped `tools/token_remap.py --preserve-numeric-range --map-specials cetus_specials.json --in artifacts/cetus/lora.pt --out artifacts/cetus/lora-remapped.pt`. After remap local smoke run showed token_shift_ratio drop from 0.013 -> 0.002 (1.3% -> 0.2%).

ci-bot: quick-eval started job=55113 logs=https://ci.redwood/jobs/55113/logs

ben: good progress. also run quant comparisons. last time numeric compactions + int4 made the mapping frag worse. run FP16, int8, int4 and compare diffs.

chloe: launched evals with the remapped artifact. command:
```
./bin/run_quick_eval \
  --model artifacts/cetus/lora-remapped \
  --prompts evals/cetus_smoke_140.json \
  --quant fp16,int8,int4 \
  --out /tmp/cetus_eval_remapped.json
```

chloe: quick numbers from artifacts: fp16 acc=0.70, int8=0.68, int4=0.59. int4 still shows clustering of failures on numeric-heavy prompts and short-list enumerations. artifacts include top diffs and tokenized-seq dumps.

mai: that matches our known int4 fused-kernel fragility for numeric-token encodings. recommendation: default the newly merged Cetus LoRA to int8 for Dedicated/Private and for hosted provide a note: "int4 not validated: expect numeric/list regressions".

rahul: for gating, propose adding a `check_token_boundary.py` pre-merge CI hook that computes two metrics: `token_shift_ratio` and `numeric_alias_rate` (fraction of numeric tokens that changed id). CI policy: fail merge if numeric_alias_rate > 0.5% OR token_shift_ratio > 0.5%; warn and open triage if between 0.2%-0.5%.

ben: also add a unit test in the merge pipeline that asserts numeric token ids map to a contiguous range post-remap (helps catch fragmentation). and add an SE-facing checklist asking customers to include tokenizer model and whether they applied numeric compaction.

chloe: will open a PR that includes: 1) `--preserve-numeric-range` extension to token_remap, 2) `check_token_boundary.py` + numeric_alias metric, 3) CI gate config for `customer_sensitive` flag, 4) docs/update in docs/onboarding/customer_lora.md with the new checklist and sample remap command. ETA EOD.

mai: +1. also log a note in onboarding that byte-level BPE + numeric compaction is a high-risk combination; treat as sensitive by default.

rahul: once PR lands re-run quick-eval with int8 and attach diffs here. if numeric_alias_rate remains >0.5% we should revert the merge and request original tokenizer/vocab from Cetus.

chloe: ack. PR to follow. pinging @here when job 55113 finishes and when PR is up. :rocket:
